tracks.title: Requiem in C minor: Introitus et Kyrie
tracks.fact: Beethoven considered Cherubini the greatest living composer of his time, and this Requiem was performed at Beethoven's funeral in 1827.

tracks.title: Médée (Medea): Overture
tracks.fact: Brahms admired the overture to Medea immensely, keeping it as a permanent reference score in his study.

tracks.title: Symphony in D major: I. Largo - Allegro molto
tracks.fact: Cherubini's only symphony was commissioned directly by the Royal Philharmonic Society in London in 1815.

tracks.title: Marche funèbre
tracks.fact: Composed in 1820 following the assassination of the Duke of Berry, noted for its unusually stark instrumentation.

tracks.title: String Quartet No. 1 in E-flat major
tracks.fact: Cherubini began writing string quartets only after turning fifty, directly modeling them on Haydn's late works.

tracks.title: Ave Maria
tracks.fact: An intimate sacred piece written for soprano and English horn during his service at the Royal Chapel in Paris.

event_note: Christmas Eve – Exquisite Baroque and Classical Christmas Masterpieces

tracks.title: Concerto Grosso in G minor, Op. 6, No. 8 'Fatto per la notte di Natale'
tracks.fact: Corelli's famous 'Christmas Concerto' was composed specifically for Christmas Eve performance and features a subtle pastoral final movement.

tracks.title: The Nutcracker: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy
tracks.fact: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was among the first to use the newly imported celesta instrument from Paris in this piece.

tracks.title: The Nutcracker: Waltz of the Flowers
tracks.fact: This grand waltz from The Nutcracker remains one of the most widely recognized orchestral ballet pieces in the world.

tracks.title: Pastorale in F major
tracks.fact: A traditional Italian Christmas melody frequently adapted by Baroque masters for holiday celebrations.

tracks.title: Hodie Christus natus est (Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck)
tracks.fact: A luminous Renaissance Christmas motet rich in intricate vocal polyphony.

tracks.title: Silent Night (Choral Version)
tracks.fact: The world's most popular carol, composed in 1818 in Austria by Franz Xaver Gruber.

event_note: Christmas Day – Monumental Baroque Sacred Masterpieces

tracks.title: Christmas Oratorio, BWV 248: Part I - Jauchzet, frohlocket
tracks.fact: The opening part of Bach's Christmas Oratorio bursts forth with powerful timpani strokes and triumphant trumpets celebrating the Nativity.

tracks.title: Christmas Oratorio, BWV 248: Pastoral Symphony (Sinfonia)
tracks.fact: An instrumental interlude introducing Part II, depicting the peaceful Bethlehem night and the watching shepherds.

tracks.title: Magnificat in D major, BWV 243: I. Magnificat anima mea
tracks.fact: Bach originally composed this brilliant setting for the Christmas vespers service in Leipzig in 1723.

tracks.title: Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme, BWV 140
tracks.fact: One of Bach's most celebrated chorale cantatas, blending deep spiritual devotion with majestic counterpoint.

tracks.title: Orchestral Suite No. 3 in D major: Air on the G String
tracks.fact: A piece of profound tranquility, offering an ideal soundtrack for a peaceful holiday morning.

tracks.title: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring
tracks.fact: Bach's iconic chorale setting brings deep inner peace and has become a permanent staple of classical holiday playlists.

event_note: Boxing Day – Monumental Choral and Orchestral Masterpieces

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: Hallelujah Chorus
tracks.fact: King George II was so moved by the power of this chorus that he stood up, inspiring the enduring tradition of audience standing.

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: For Unto Us a Child Is Born
tracks.fact: A joyous chorus from Messiah adapted from an Italian secular duet into a monumental sacred masterpiece.

tracks.title: Water Music: Suite in F major, HWV 348: Allegro
tracks.fact: First performed on a barge on the River Thames for the British monarch, exuding festive brilliance and courtly elegance.

tracks.title: Music for the Royal Fireworks: La Rejouissance
tracks.fact: Commissioned by the King for the public celebration of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, featuring an imposing wind band.

tracks.title: Messiah, HWV 56: Pastoral Symphony
tracks.fact: Another exquisite pastoral movement within our holiday collection, setting a contemplative and atmospheric mood.

tracks.title: Zadok the Priest (Coronation Anthem)
tracks.fact: Handel composed this anthem for the coronation of George II in 1727; it has since been performed at every British coronation.
